title: The decision code, final call, action and outcome values and the payload placement of an archive or purge record are in no source
source: RWB-E1-017 sections 4, 7, 11 and 12; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 to A2.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03
description: The legacy story records the run at job-run level (counts per product and table, rule version, archive location, hold report) and names no decision code. TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives decision_log_entry a decision_code from LOV-DECISION, rule_version, inputs_ref, recommendation, actions and outcome, but T3.2 does not enumerate LOV-DECISION, and no source states which code and final call an archive or purge action carries or which of the fields carries the run reference, the product and table, the counts archived and kept, the hold report reference and the archive location.
evidence: RWB-E1-017 section 4 step 9 and section 12 (job run checks with counts, rule version, archive location and hold report; Events published None); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 decision_code, DF-DEC-008 inputs_ref, DF-DEC-009 recommendation, DF-DEC-012 final_call, DF-DEC-014 actions, DF-DEC-015 outcome; T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT only; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 (an unknown decision code is refused) with no list.
proposed: Take the decision code and final call from LOV-DECISION and the final-call list in force through the rwb-case reference-data contract, keep ruleId empty, put the run reference in inputsRef and the product, table, counts, hold report reference and archive location in actions and outcome, and settle the value names with the reference-data owner before the first joint environment.

title: The text of MSG-P7-009 and the ids and texts of the not-found answer, the chain-break report and the collection gap alert are not written in any source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1, A2.2.4.3 and A2.5.4.3; RWB-E1-017 sections 5 and 14; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s14
description: The FSD names MSG-P7-009 as the message of a record refused at the schema check, and the 404, the break report and the gap alert as outcomes, without writing their text or allocating an id to three of them. Section 14 therefore carries four messages with a written text and three outcomes whose id and text stand as the placeholder.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 (refused with message MSG-P7-009 naming the field, text not written); AC-EXC-P7-001-01 and AC-BG-P7-001-01 (a break is reported the same day, report text and id absent); RWB-E1-017 section 14 lists MSG-P1-020, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P1-002, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P2-006 and MSG-P4-002 only.
proposed: Write the four texts once with the P7 business analyst, keep MSG-P7-009 as the carrier of the schema and exclusion refusals, and keep the legacy AC8 check name inside it character for character.

title: The JOB-14 timezone, page size, overlap and catch-up values, the property names and the behaviour of the feature flag when off are in no source
source: Architecture v5 slides 44 and 28 through the P7 context pack; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01; TSD P7 v2 T7 (NFR-035); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10
description: Architecture v5 slide 44 fixes JOB-14 as a daily 02:00 Schedule and slide 28 fixes a collection and seal expectation, and no source states the timezone, the page size of the chain read, the overlap and catch-up policy of the Schedule, the names of the properties that carry them or what a reader sees when the feature flag is off.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-14 Hash-chain check, daily 02:00, owner rwb-decision, mechanism Schedule) and slide 28 (collect and seal) as repeated in the context pack; TSD P7 v2 NFR-035 (daily check, same-day report) with no parameter values; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01 (nightly, break reported the same day).
proposed: Run JOB-14 at 02:00 Asia/Bangkok on queue rwb-decision with page size 5000 and an overlap policy that allows one run at a time; treat the property names and the flag-off answer as configuration decisions recorded in the service template.

title: The eight patterns add five platform build dependencies, one reference-data contract and one authorise contract that the metadata rows of a secondary slice do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03, DP-07, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.4; P7 context pack ownership rows; Work Package B2-P7-008 story line (H [], C [RWB-P1-E1017-CON], I [], X [])
description: The patterns the Work Package fixes for this story add H rows RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, a C row RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the P4 authorise contract of DP-11, while the story line fixes Depends on (build) empty and RWB-P1-E1017-CON as the only contract dependency. The metadata rows are written exactly as the Work Package fixes them, and the added rows are carried in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-10 (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), DP-15 (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and DP-11 (a C from the legacy dependency); the Work Package fixes H [], C [RWB-P1-E1017-CON], I [], X [] and marks the slice secondary.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the delivery lead
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the Work Package fixes them, name every added row in the pattern table and the fakes of 12.8, build against the published contracts and fakes from Day 1, and let step D1 decide whether the five H rows and the three consumed contracts enter the dependency map.

title: The name of the rwb-decision database login is in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules
description: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and no document states the login name, its role name or its credential scope, so the story uses the phrase 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and registers the value as missing.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R4 (one login per service) and R5.5 DP-02 (recovery_svc login becomes one login per service); P7 context pack 'Naming and shared platform rules' names the schema, the base, the topic, the queue and the package, and no login.
proposed: Let the ACE team allocate the login with the schema rwb_decision and record it in the platform secret store; the story keeps the phrase until it is allocated.

title: The story file at the Work Package path already existed as a partial artefact of the superseded Work Package B-P7-05, with no fragment, no register rows and citations that resolve to nothing
source: Work Package B2-P7-008 Write only list; _work/msr/status.json (B-P7-05 SUPERSEDED, stopped for the B2 split queue); _work/msr/fragments (no RWB-P7-E1017-APP.json before this Work Package); _work/msr/gaps and _work/msr/assumptions (no CG-B-P7-05-E1017 row)
description: A 69,993-byte story file stood at this story's path, written for the same story key by the superseded Work Package B-P7-05. It carried citations CG-B-P7-05-E1017-1 to -7 and ASM-B-P7-05-E1017-1 to -7, and no gap or assumption row of that Work Package exists, so none of the fourteen citations resolved; the fragment of the story and the edit log of the producing Work Package were also absent, and the file stood at about three times the size aim of the Work Package.
evidence: File length 69,993 bytes and modification time 22 November 2026 17:54; status.json entry for B-P7-05 ('state': 'SUPERSEDED', 'note': 'stopped for the B2 split queue'); no gaps/B-P7-05.jsonl and no editlog/B-P7-05.md in the workspace; no fragment RWB-P7-E1017-APP.json before this Work Package wrote it.
owner_role: Delivery lead, with the traceability owner
proposed: This Work Package writes the file at its fixed path from the legacy story and the P7 module sources, with the citations of this Work Package and a size near the aim; the substance of the partial artefact is carried forward and no orphan citation is left in the tree.

title: A secondary slice with an empty acceptance-criteria list owns no legacy criterion while its ten legacy test cases are kept
source: Work Package B2-P7-008 story line (secondary true, acs []); Template and Rules v1 R5.7, R7.2 s7 and s16; RWB-E1-017 section 7 and section 16
description: The story line fixes acs empty, so the nine legacy criteria of RWB-E1-017 belong to RWB-P1-E1017-APP, RWB-P5-E1017-APP and RWB-ITG-E1017-ITG, while the ten legacy test case IDs are carried in tcs_legacy and kept. The Covers column therefore names this slice's new criteria, and the mapping from the legacy System and Access levels to the levels of R7.2 is a ruling of this story.
evidence: Work Package story line for RWB-P7-E1017-APP (acs [], tcs_legacy TC-E1-017-01 to TC-E1-017-10); RWB-E1-017 section 7 (AC1 to AC9) and section 16 (ten test cases, Level System and Access); Template and Rules v1 R5.7 rule 2 and R7.2 s16.
proposed: Keep the ten legacy test case IDs in their legacy order with the Covers column naming this slice's criteria, map System to Component, Contract or End to end and Access to Contract, and leave the legacy criteria with the slices that own them and with the wave 1 integration story.
